decisions.title: Host Hermes on a Hetzner CX22 instead of the Raspberry Pi
decisions.context: The Pi kept corrupting its SD card and couldn't run the embedding model for vault search.
decisions.reasoning: CX22 is cheap, EU-hosted, has enough RAM for SQLite + embeddings, and snapshots make backups trivial. Tailscale removes the need for a public endpoint.
alternatives: Keep the Raspberry Pi with an SSD hat

decisions.title: The phone app gets exactly one write endpoint (capture)
decisions.context: Designing the Lens API contract — how much should the phone be able to change?
decisions.reasoning: The agent owns the vault; the phone is a lens. Capture plus queued flag/triage requests keep the failure surface tiny and make the API trivial to secure and reimplement.

decisions.title: Rewrite the novel in third person limited
decisions.context: First-person voice collapsed once the second POV character appeared in chapter 5.
decisions.reasoning: Third limited keeps the intimacy but allows POV switches per chapter. Costs a two-day rewrite of chapters 1–2, saves the structure.

decisions.title: Pause the renovation until written landlord approval
decisions.context: Contractor pushed to start next month; Hale only approved verbally.
decisions.reasoning: Verbal approval is worthless if the lease ends in dispute. The quote stays valid three more weeks, so waiting costs nothing yet.

decisions.title: Register for B1, not B2
decisions.context: Rosa assessed current level as strong A2/weak B1 after mock test #1.
decisions.reasoning: A certain B1 pass in autumn beats a risky B2. The certificate matters for the evening-course application; the level itself matters less.
alternatives: B2 with an intensive summer course

decisions.title: Build Hermes Lens as a Capacitor SPA, not a native app
decisions.context: Choosing the stack for the phone dashboard.
decisions.reasoning: One TypeScript codebase, the whole data layer is shared with the future web view, and native surface is only needed for biometrics and the widget. I can ship it alone in evenings.
